assumptions: The /admin/run-task endpoint is reachable to an attacker who can send HTTP POST requests (for example, from elsewhere on the internal network or via a compromised internal service).

The attacker can obtain or guess a valid X-Internal-Token value, such as the default 'dev-insecure-token' in environments where OMNICORE_INTERNAL_TOKEN is not securely set, or via leakage/misconfiguration in higher environments.
The service process runs with sufficient privileges that executing arbitrary shell commands on the host is security-relevant (e.g., access to sensitive data, the network, or other services).
No external web application firewall or reverse proxy is stripping or strictly validating the 'cmd' field in a way that would reliably prevent shell metacharacter injection.
vulnerability_candidate.description: Remote command execution via the /admin/run-task endpoint: the handler takes a JSON body field 'cmd', coerces lists into a space-joined string, and executes it with shell=True via subprocess.check_output without any server-side validation or whitelisting. Access is gated only by a static header token, which defaults to a hard-coded 'dev-insecure-token' when the environment variable is not set. An attacker who can reach this endpoint and provide a valid X-Internal-Token can inject arbitrary shell commands.
